title: What If the World Ran Out of Copper? The 43-Year Myth

scenes.text: What if the world ran out of copper? The famous number says 43 years. It's misleading.
Miners dig up about 23 million tons of copper a year, per the US Geological Survey.
Known reserves are about 980 million tons. That works out to roughly 43 years at today's pace.
But reserves are only what's profitable to mine today, not what's left in the ground.
Identified resources hold about 2.1 billion tons, and undiscovered deposits may add 3.5 billion more.
So the real limit is cost and new mines, not the ground. The 43 years is a snapshot, not a deadline.

description:
What if the world ran out of copper?
The 43-year figure comes from dividing today's reserves by today's mining, but the USGS says resources are far larger.
